arxiv-1801-06181.title: On Determining Dead Layer and Detector Thicknesses for a Position-Sensitive Silicon Detector Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research
arxiv-1801-06181.creator: J. Manfredi, Jenny Lee, W.G. Lynch, C.Y. Niu, M.B. Tsang, C. Anderson, J. Barney, K.W. Brown, Z. Chajecki, K.P. Chan, G. Chen, J. Estee, Z. Li, C. Pruitt, A.M. Rogers, A. Sanetullaev, H. Setiawan, R. Showalter, C.Y. Tsang, J.R. Winkelbauer, Z. Xiao, Z. Xu
arxiv-1801-06181.description: Abstract In this work, two particular properties of the position-sensitive, thick silicon detectors (known as the “E” detectors) in the High Resolution Array (HiRA) are investigated: the thickness of the dead layer on the front of the detector, and the overall thickness of the detector itself.

arxiv-2012-07121.title: Deliberative and Conceptual Inference in Service Robots
arxiv-2012-07121.creator: Luis A. Pineda, Noé Hernández, Arturo Rodríguez, Ricardo Cruz, Gibrán Fuentes
arxiv-2012-07121.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Luis A. Pineda, Noé Hernández, Arturo Rodríguez, Ricardo Cruz, Gibrán Fuentes. Service robots need to reason to support people in daily life situations. Reasoning is an expensive resource that should be used on demand whenever the expectations of the robot do not match the situation of the world and the execution of the task is broken down; in such scenarios the robot must perform the common sense daily life inference cycle consisting on diagnosing what happened, deciding what to do about it, and inducing

arxiv-2210-09633.title: Observational constraints on accelerators of ultra-high energy cosmic rays
arxiv-2210-09633.creator: Sullivan Marafico, Jonathan Biteau, Antonio Condorelli, Olivier Deligny, Quentin Luce
arxiv-2210-09633.description: Abstract We explore two generic hypotheses for tracing the sources of ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) in the Universe: star formation rate density or stellar mass density. For each scenario, we infer a set of constraints for the emission mechanisms in the accelerators, for their energetics and for the abundances of elements at escape from their environments.

arxiv-2210-16758.title: The correspondence between the canonical and semicanonical bases Thanks: Jiepeng Fang and Yixin Lan were supported by Tsinghua University Initiative Scientific Research Program (No. 2019Z07L01006), and Jie Xiao was supported by NSF of China (No. 12031007).
arxiv-2210-16758.creator: Jiepeng Fang,Yixin Lan,Jie Xiao
arxiv-2210-16758.description: Abstract . Given any symmetric Cartan datum, Lusztig has provided in [ 11 ] and [ 9 ] a pair of key lemmas to construct the perverse sheaves over the corresponding quiver and the functions of irreducible components over the corresponding preprojective algebra respectively. In the present article, we prove that these two inductive algorithms of Lusztig coincide.

arxiv-2302-01862.title: Low-depth simulations of fermionic systems on square-grid quantum hardware
arxiv-2302-01862.creator: Manuel G. Algaba, P.V. Sriluckshmy, Martin Leib, Fedor Šimkovic IV
arxiv-2302-01862.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Manuel G. Algaba, P.V. Sriluckshmy, Martin Leib, Fedor Šimkovic IV. We present a general strategy for mapping fermionic systems to NISQ hardware with square qubit connectivity which yields low-depth quantum circuits, counted in the number of native two-qubit fSIM gates. We achieve this by leveraging novel operator decomposition and circuit compression techniques paired with specifically chosen low-depth fermion-to-qubit mappings and allow for a high degree of gate cancellations and parallelism.

arxiv-2303-07663.title: Interface Response Functions for multicomponent alloy solidification- An application to additive manufacturing Journal: Computational Materials Science
arxiv-2303-07663.creator: V S Hariharan, B S Murty, Gandham Phanikumar
arxiv-2303-07663.description: Abstract The near-rapid solidification conditions during additive manufacturing can lead to selection of non-equilibrium phases. Sharp interface models via interface response functions have been used earlier to explain the microstructure selection under such solidification conditions. However, most of the sharp interface models assume linear superposition of contributions of alloying elements without considering the non-linearity associated with the phase diagram.

arxiv-2312-10531.title: How to Train Neural Field Representations: A Comprehensive Study and Benchmark
arxiv-2312-10531.creator: Samuele Papa, Riccardo Valperga, David Knigge, Miltiadis Kofinas, Phillip Lippe, Jan-Jakob Sonke, Efstratios Gavves
arxiv-2312-10531.description: Abstract Neural fields (NeFs) have recently emerged as a versatile method for modeling signals of various modalities, including images, shapes, and scenes. Subsequently, a number of works have explored the use of NeFs as representations for downstream tasks, e.g. classifying an image based on the parameters of a NeF that has been fit to it.

arxiv-2405-19096.title: The Precise Complexity of Reasoning in ALC with Omega-Admissible Concrete Domains (Extended Version)
arxiv-2405-19096.creator: Stefan Borgwardt, Filippo De Bortoli, Patrick Koopmann
arxiv-2405-19096.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Stefan Borgwardt, Filippo De Bortoli, Patrick Koopmann. Concrete domains have been introduced in the context of Description Logics to allow references to qualitative and quantitative values. In particular, the class of ω \omega -admissible concrete domains, which includes Allen’s interval algebra, the region connection calculus (RCC8), and the rational numbers with ordering and equality, has been shown to yield extensions of 𝒜 ​ ℒ ​ 𝒞 \mathcal{ALC} for which concept satisfiability w.r.t. a general TBox is decidable.

arxiv-2408-11422.title: Scenario-Based Robust Optimization of Tree Structures Thanks: Partially supported by the grant ANR-23-CE48-0010 PREDICTIONS from the French National Research Agency (ANR).
arxiv-2408-11422.creator: Spyros Angelopoulos, Christoph Dürr, Alex Elenter, Georgii Melidi
arxiv-2408-11422.description: Abstract We initiate the study of tree structures in the context of scenario -based robust optimization. Specifically, we study Binary Search Trees (BSTs) and Huffman coding, two fundamental techniques for efficiently managing and encoding data based on a known set of frequencies of keys.

arxiv-2410-21642.title: Local bi-integrability of bi-Hamiltonian systems, Part II: Real smooth case
arxiv-2410-21642.creator: I. K. Kozlov
arxiv-2410-21642.description: Abstract We prove that any bi-Hamiltonian system v = ( 𝒜 + λ ​ ℬ ) ​ d ​ H λ v=\left(\mathcal{A}+\lambda\mathcal{B}\right)dH_{\lambda} on a real smooth manifold that is Hamiltonian with respect all Poisson brackets ( 𝒜 + λ ​ ℬ ) \left(\mathcal{A}+\lambda\mathcal{B}\right) is locally bi-integrable.

arxiv-2411-18720.title: Responsivity and Stability of Nonlinear Exceptional Point Lasers with Saturable Gain and Loss
arxiv-2411-18720.creator: Todd Darcie, J. Stewart Aitchison
arxiv-2411-18720.description: Abstract The responsivity of perturbation sensing can be effectively enhanced by using higher-order exceptional points (HOEPs) due to their nonlinear response to frequency perturbations. However, experimental realization can be difficult due to the stringent parameter conditions associated with these points.

arxiv-2509-09438.title: GrACE: A Generative Approach to Better Confidence Elicitation in Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-09438.creator: Zhaohan Zhang, Ziquan Liu, Ioannis Patras
arxiv-2509-09438.description: Abstract Assessing the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) by confidence elicitation is a prominent approach to AI safety in high-stakes applications, such as healthcare and finance. Existing methods either require expensive computational overhead or suffer from poor calibration, making them impractical and unreliable for real-world deployment.

arxiv-2509-10609.title: Assembling GW231123 in star clusters through the combination of stellar binary evolution and hierarchical mergers Facilities: Simulations are ran on the MERAC2A high-performance computing workstation, hosted at GSSI and financially supported through the MERAC 2023 Prize awarded by the European Astro
arxiv-2509-10609.creator: Lavinia Paiella, Cristiano Ugolini, Mario Spera, Marica Branchesi, Manuel Arca Sedda
arxiv-2509-10609.description: Abstract GW231123 is the most massive binary black hole (BBH) merger detected to date by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration. With at least one black hole (BH) in the upper-mass gap and both BHs exhibiting high spins ( χ 1 , 2 ≳ 0.8 \chi_{1,2}\gtrsim 0.8 ), this event challenges standard isolated binary evolution models.

arxiv-2511-07615.title: On measures derived from orbital integrals Thanks: The author was supported by IAM-CONICET, grants PIP 2010-0757 (CONICET) and PICT 2010-2478 (ANPCyT)
arxiv-2511-07615.creator: Martin Miglioli
arxiv-2511-07615.description: Abstract . In this article we propose a novel framework to derive piecewise polynomial measures which result from invariant measures on adjoint orbits in the general context of compact and semi-simple Lie groups. The measures are computed from orbital integrals by a series of transformations on spaces of polynomials endowed with the apolar inner product. Keywords.

arxiv-2511-14673.title: Closing in on 𝜶 \alpha -attractors
arxiv-2511-14673.creator: David Wands
arxiv-2511-14673.description: Abstract Recent observations of cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies combined with large-scale structure may point towards higher values of the scalar spectral index, n s n_{s} . This puts previously preferred inflationary models, such as α \alpha -attractors, in tension with the new measurements.

pmc-11696749.title: Deep Multitask Learning-Driven Discovery of New Compounds Targeting Leishmania infantum
pmc-11696749.creator: Eder Soares
pmc-11696749.description: Visceral leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania infantum is a severe and often fatal disease prevalent in low- and middle-income countries. Existing treatments are hampered by toxicity, high costs, and the emergence of drug resistance, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutics.

pmc-13550414.title: HMMR+ stromal cells drive human uterine development
pmc-13550414.creator: Jiahui Qi, Xiaoqiang Sheng, Shiyuan Li, Peipei Jiang, Huiyan Wang, Lingxi Li, Jidong Zhou, Yifan Li, Huidan Zhang, Miaomiao Wang, Yang Zhang, Guangfeng Zhao, Guijun Yan, Bruno Péault, Yali Hu, Haixiang Sun, Lijun Ding
pmc-13550414.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Early uterine development in humans is a critical determinant of reproductive health and disease susceptibility during adolescence. While single-cell analyses have extensively characterized the adult uterus, the developmental origins of this organ remain poorly understood. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of the human uterus from gestational week 12 (GW12) to GW24 and from adolescents revealed a population of hyaluronan-mediated motility receptor-expressing (HMMR+) stromal cells essential for uterine endometrial and myometrial development.

pmc-13557068.title: TCR-JANUS engager proteins enable bispecific targeting to overcome tumor heterogeneity in TCR-T cell therapy
pmc-13557068.creator: Chenxi Cheng, Ting Liang, Pengju Yao, Wenling Wang, Huxuan Chen, Xiaowen Li, Ying Tian, Jie Wang, Ni Yan, Danli Xie, Fuming Qiu, Shuguang Tan
pmc-13557068.description: T cell receptor (TCR)–based immunotherapy is limited by tumor antigen heterogeneity, which frequently leads to relapse. We developed a bispecific TCR-JANUS engager that functions synergistically with TCR engineered T cells (TCR-T). In contrast to conventional T cell engagers targeting CD3, TCR-JANUS engages both the variable region of a transgenic TCR (TRBV) and a tumor surface antigen.
